themes.title: Context management
themes.subtitle: Treat the context window like a budget — top-rated tip across every source.

tips.headline: Use /clear between unrelated tasks
tips.body: Every time you start something new, clear the chat. Old history eats tokens and forces Claude to run compaction summaries that degrade reasoning. Steve Sewell (builder.io) and ykdojo's tips repo (8.1k★) both rank this #1.

sources.label: builder.io — My best Claude Code tips

tips.headline: Proactively /compact before you hit the wall
tips.body: Don't wait for auto-compaction. Run /compact "keep only the failing-test traces and the file paths I'm editing" so the summary keeps what matters. Auto-compaction loses crucial detail.

tips.headline: Keep CLAUDE.md short and review it monthly
tips.body: Long CLAUDE.md files crowd out task context and contradict themselves. Keep it under ~50 lines: project quirks, build/test commands, conventions. Re-read and prune monthly.

tips.headline: Slim the system prompt by ~50%
tips.body: Drop tool descriptions you'll never use (e.g. mcp servers you don't have configured). ykdojo reports cutting the system prompt roughly in half with no quality loss — and a measurable speed boost.

themes.title: Plan first, execute second
themes.subtitle: The single biggest leverage move per HN front-page consensus.

tips.headline: Separate planning from execution
tips.body: Run a planning pass (or use Plan Mode) that produces a written plan in markdown before any file edits. Boris Tane's writeup hit #1 on HN with 976 points making this exact case: planning prevents 'first-attempt-95%-garbage' rewrites.

sources.label: boristane.com — How I use Claude Code

tips.headline: Break big problems into A→A1→A2→B steps
tips.body: When Claude can't one-shot a task, force decomposition: 'break this into the smallest sub-problems you can independently verify.' Each sub-problem gets its own short context window.

tips.headline: Use 'planning-with-files' (markdown plan persistence)
tips.body: OthmanAdi/planning-with-files (20.7k★) is a skill that has Claude write plans to disk, tick boxes as it works, and survive /compact and /clear. Adopted as the standard pattern for multi-hour tasks.

themes.title: Verification & TDD
themes.subtitle: If Claude can't verify, it'll happily lie. Wire up feedback loops.

tips.headline: Write tests first; let Claude make them pass
tips.body: TDD turns vague specs into machine-checkable contracts. Claude excels at the green→refactor cycle when the red test is hand-written and the failure message is clear.

tips.headline: Always close the write-test cycle for autonomous tasks
tips.body: Before walking away from a long-running session, make sure Claude can run the test command itself and observe the output. Without a feedback loop it'll declare victory while broken.

tips.headline: Master multiple verification modes
tips.body: Beyond unit tests: have it run the script, screenshot the UI (Chrome integration), curl the endpoint, or diff against golden output. One mode is brittle; three modes catch nearly everything.

tips.headline: Talk to it with your voice
tips.body: Local Whisper/Parakeet transcription is faster than typing for instructions. Even with transcription errors Claude reads through them. Built-in voice mode shipped recently; many still prefer local for latency.

tips.headline: Customize the status line to show token-usage bar
tips.body: Add a context-bar.sh status line showing model + branch + uncommitted file count + token-usage progress bar. Stops you from over-running context unintentionally.

tips.headline: Use git worktrees for parallel branch work
tips.body: Spawn one Claude session per worktree so two features can be developed concurrently without context-switching the model. Pairs well with multiple terminal tabs.

tips.headline: Run risky long jobs in containers
tips.body: For tasks that could touch your filesystem broadly (large refactors, dependency upgrades), run Claude inside a docker container with the repo mounted. Easy to throw away on bad outcomes.

themes.title: Permissions & safety
themes.subtitle: Two camps: 'allow-list everything' vs '--dangerously-skip-permissions'. Pick consciously.

tips.headline: Audit your approved-commands list
tips.body: Run claude config and review the commands you've blanket-approved. People accumulate Bash(rm:*) and similar by accident. Trim quarterly.

tips.headline: If you use --dangerously-skip-permissions, do it in a container or worktree
tips.body: Steve Sewell's take: 'Could a rogue agent run a destructive command? Sure. Have I seen it? Never.' But the safer version is to skip permissions only inside a sandboxed worktree or container.

tips.headline: Use --allowedTools / --disallowedTools per-session
tips.body: For specific runs, narrow the surface: --allowedTools 'Bash(git:*)' 'Write' --disallowedTools 'Bash(rm:*)' 'Bash(sudo:*)'. Reduces surprise prompts without going fully YOLO.

themes.title: Skills, sub-agents, and MCP
themes.subtitle: Where Claude Code differentiates from competitors.

tips.headline: Know the four extension surfaces
tips.body: CLAUDE.md = always-loaded preferences. Skills = LLM-loaded procedures (markdown). Slash commands = user-typed shortcuts. Plugins = bundled hooks+commands+skills. Don't conflate them — pick the lightest one that fits.

tips.headline: Adopt one curated subagent collection rather than rolling your own
tips.body: VoltAgent/awesome-claude-code-subagents (19.5k★) ships 100+ specialist agents (security-reviewer, refactorer, sql-tuner). Cheaper than reinventing.

tips.headline: Install the dx plugin for one-shot ergonomics
tips.body: ykdojo's dx plugin bundles status line, context bar, common slash commands, and worktree helpers in one install — reasonable starting kit if you don't want to assemble manually.

tips.headline: Use a context-reduction MCP server to slash token bills
tips.body: mksg.lu/blog/context-mode reports an MCP server that cuts Claude Code context consumption by 98% on large repos by lazy-loading file contents. Front-paged HN with 570 points last quarter.

tips.headline: Over-broad prompts in massive repos
tips.body: 'Refactor the auth system' against a 200k-line monorepo will burn tokens before producing anything. Always scope: 'in src/auth/middleware/ only, ...'

tips.headline: Letting one long session run for hours
tips.body: After ~3 hours the conversation drifts. Multiple HN threads flag this. Branch off with /clear (or fork the conversation) when context starts feeling stale.

tips.headline: Skipping git commit between Claude steps
tips.body: Commit after every meaningful Claude-generated diff. It's the cheapest undo and the cheapest checkpoint to feed back as 'what changed since X' for the next prompt.
